title: Two short brackets, one above the other
description: The generic Bulgarian pole top: a plain concrete pole carrying two short brackets at different heights, each with a single upright insulator. The commonest arrangement in the country, so it settles little on its own — it is the baseline the other variants depart from.

title: Black sleeving on the wires at the pole
description: Black material wrapped around the conductors where they pass the pole. Puts you in eastern Bulgaria, and more often than not in the south-east.

title: Bracket with a long triangular stay
description: Pole top whose insulator bracket is braced from below by a triangular stay running well down the pole — longer than the usual one. Western Bulgaria. Several variants of it exist, so check the length before committing.

title: Triangular stay stopping halfway
description: Looks like the western bracket, but the triangular stay under it stops around halfway instead of running to the end. Much rarer, and tied to no particular region so far — a shape to rule out rather than to click on.

title: Very slim insulator
description: Unusually thin insulator on the bracket. Mainly eastern Bulgaria, which is also where the wires carry black sleeving, so the two usually turn up together. It does exist in the west: with no black sleeving, find another clue before committing to the east.

title: Bracket stayed at a sharp angle
description: Pole top whose brackets are braced by this distinctive support meeting the pole at a sharp angle. South-eastern Bulgaria.

title: Insulators hanging below the arms
description: Pole top where the insulators hang under the arms instead of standing on top of them. Nearly always north-eastern Bulgaria.

title: Tall slim ladder-type pole
description: The slim concrete ladder pole, seen here in open country. On the evidence gathered so far these sit in the north, above the central mountains — the author flags that more research is needed to confirm it.

title: Concrete pole pierced with rectangular holes
description: Pole with a column of rectangular openings running down its face. Highly concentrated around Veliko Tarnovo, with exceptions north-east of Shumen and around Sofia.

title: Wider version of the holed pole
description: The same pole pierced with rectangular openings, but noticeably wider. This is the version found around Sofia.

title: Long stay running down from the bracket
description: Insulator bracket braced by a stay that runs a long way down the pole. The ordinary version of the extended stay: north-west Bulgaria, from just east of Pleven to the far north-west.

title: Thicker stay under the bracket
description: The other version of the extended stay — hard to tell apart, but the member under the bracket is considerably thicker. Found so far only south-west of Sofia.

title: Square supports under hanging insulators
description: Arms carrying hanging insulators, braced by supports that close into squares. Mostly just east of Ruse, with one exception in Sofia.

title: Long support under hanging insulators
description: Arms with hanging insulators braced by a single long support. From Ruse to Dobrich, and more commonly around Dobrich. Seen only with these two disc insulators.

title: Two spread supports crossing past the pole
description: Like the long support, but the two metal supports are set further apart and carry on past the pole to the other side. In this version they sit under the main arm holding the insulators: Shumen to Dobrich.

title: Spread supports with large glass discs
description: The same spread supports, here with large glass disc insulators hanging from the arms. Around Dobrich, with one exception north of Stevrek.

title: Supports below the arm, hanging insulators
description: Arms with hanging insulators whose supports are fixed below the arm rather than above it. Around Shumen.

title: Long support under upward-facing insulators
description: Brackets holding upright insulators, braced by a single long support. Three separate areas: Varna, Stara Zagora and Ruse.

title: Mini support under upward-facing insulators
description: Brackets holding upright insulators on a much shorter support. From Pavlikeni to Tervel, mostly east of Ruse, with an exception around Pernik. At a distance or an angle it is easily confused with the long support — around Ruse either is a fair bet, since both are commonest there.

title: Two supports above the arm
description: Bracket braced by a pair of supports sitting above the main arm. Mostly around Dobrich, with an exception between Varna and Shumen, and also found around Plovdiv and Stara Zagora.

title: Two supports below the arm
description: The same doubled bracing, but with the supports below the main arm. Puts you west of Varna.

title: Support with a bend in it
description: Bracket support that bends partway along, so the two sections read as distinct. Found around Haskovo.

title: Square supports with upward-facing insulators
description: Brackets whose bracing closes into a square, here with upright insulators — very rare in that combination. From Pleven to just north of Shumen.

title: South-eastern support with only the lower stay
description: The south-eastern bracket support reduced to its bottom member alone. Between Nova Zagora and east of Yambol.

title: Seven-sided white sticker on the back of road signs
description: Small white sticker with seven sides, stuck on the reverse of road signs. Mostly the far south, with some exceptions north of Dulovo. The author flags this one as needing more research.

title: Spread supports with very small discs
description: The same two spread supports crossing past the pole, but the insulators hanging from the arms are stacks of very small discs instead of the large glass ones. Rarer than the large-disc version and more dependable: found only around Dobrich.
